In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: can we explain neutrino data and baryon asymmetry of the Universe within the minimal seesaw mechanism?

a systematic study of neutrino masses and mixings in the framework of the standard model with three right-handed neutrinos, and with the constraints on the properties of these neutrino states coming from leptogenesis.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the seesaw mechanism in its simplest form is not compatible with the observed baryon-to-photons ratio.
the seesaw mechanism is consistent with the current data and can account for the observed baryon asymmetry of the universe only in the 2-3 crossing case, which is not supported by the data.
, in the case of hierarchical Dirac-type masses, a successful baryo/leptogenesis is only possible if the level crossing point 1-2 is realized and M1,M2 ≈ 108-1010 GeV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the seesaw mechanism is consistent with the low-energy neutrino oscillation data and with leptogenesis if the neutrino Yukawas are hierarchical, the Dirac-type neutrinos are quasi-degenerate and the lightest right-handed neutrino mass is in the range 108−1010 GeV.

the seesaw mechanism can explain the observed neutrino data and can account for the baryon asymmetry of the Universe only for special cases, with the lightest right-handed neutrino mass in the range 103−106GeV and the second right-handed neutrino with a mass of the order 108 GeV.

the seesaw mechanism can accommodate the observed neutrino masses and the observed baryon asymmetry only if the masses of the lightest two right-handed neutrinos satisfy the 1-3 level crossing conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the seesaw mechanism and baryogenesis via the leptogenesis mechanism can be reconciled if the light neutrinos are Dirac-type, the lightest heavy neutrino is quasi-degenerate with the second one, the masses are in the range of 108 GeV, and the mass differences are in the range (M2− M1)/M1 ≈ 10−5.

the seesaw model with three right-handed Majorana fermions can accommodate the current neutrino data and at the same time explain the baryon asymmetry of the Universe, if the neutrino Yukawas are such that the level crossing point is reached.
the seesaw mechanism and leptogenesis can be tested in the future high energy collider experiments, in particular in the Large Hadron Collider.
